# Publication information
## Michelle C. Agne, Robert A. Slesak, Constance A. Harrington, Beth A. Roskilly, Kristen L. Chadwick, Melissa Fischer
## Assisted population migration of Douglas-fir using operational transfer guidelines has limited risk to tree health
## Ecological Applications
### In review / revision

# Purpose and methods
This script fits all candidate models and performs model selection for models of climate transfer distance effects on eight tree health indicator response variables. All tree health indicators were simplified to binary (presence/absence) variables. Resulting models assessed probability of a given tree health indicator, and were therefore fit with a binomial distribution and logit link.

Candidate models were fit with transfer distance for one temperature-related variable (MCMT, MWMT, or MAT), one precipitation-related variable (MAP, MSP, or SHM), and temperature differential (TD, also known as continentality index). For each term in the model, the quadratic version of the term was also included. Climate variables were checked for multicollinearity prior to model fitting.

All three-way and two-way combinations were fit as well as all single term models and a random effects only model, resulting in 30 candidate models per response variable. 

All candidate models also included a random effect for seed source region as well as nested random effects of plot within block within site. 
Exceptions: crown transparency models only included a random effect for seed source and a random effect of site due to model convergence issues with additional nested random effects (in all candidate models). Sunken bole only included a random effect for seed source region and nested random effects of  block within site due to model convergence issues with additional nested random effect (in all candidate models).

All models were evaluated for convergence prior to model selection. Models that did not converge were excluded from model selection. The remaining models for each response variable were compared using AIC. We selected the model with the lowest AIC, although all models within deltaAIC of 2 were considered as equally "good" models. When there were multiple models within 2 deltaAIC, we selected the form that minimized the number of non-significant terms in the model while retaining significant predictors.

Model output and visualization are available in TreeHealth_ClimTransfer.Rmd - this script generates the output Table S2

```{r, include=FALSE}
#load packages
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(corrplot)
library(broom)
library(broom.mixed)
library(DHARMa)
library(viridis)
library(ggpubr)
library(AICcmodavg)
library(knitr)
library(ggstatsplot)
library(ggeffects)
library(patchwork)
library(lme4)
```


# Read in climate and field data
```{r, include=FALSE}
field_climate_08_23_inc <- read.csv("field_climate_08_23_w18_21_growth_NSavgs.csv", row.names=1, na.strings="NA")%>%
  mutate(SHM_mult_dist = (-1*(1 - (SHM/Site_SHM)))*100)%>% #calculate the SHM transfer distance in terms of percent 
  mutate(SHM_mult_dist = round(SHM_mult_dist, digits=3))%>%
  mutate(MAT_dist_sq = MAT_dist^2,
         MAP_dist_sq = MAP_dist^2,
         MCMT_dist_sq = MCMT_dist^2,
         TD_dist_sq = TD_dist^2,
         MSP_dist_sq = MSP_dist^2,
         MWMT_dist_sq = MWMT_dist^2,
         CMD_dist_sq = CMD_dist^2,
         CMI_dist_sq = CMI_dist^2,
         SHM_mult_dist_sq = SHM_mult_dist^2) 
```

# Read in standardized forest health metrics
```{r}
live_trees_w_homesource <- read.csv("live_trees_w_homesource.csv", row.names=1, na.strings="NA")
```

## Join
```{r}
live_trees_cond <- live_trees_w_homesource %>% dplyr::select(S, PLT, TAG, STEM:Gall_diff)

field_climate_08_23 <- right_join(field_climate_08_23_inc,live_trees_cond, by=c("S","PLT","TAG")) %>%
  mutate(SITE_NAME = as.factor(SITE_NAME))
```

## Standardize all predictors
```{r, echo=FALSE}
field_climate_08_23$Site_MCMT_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_MCMT - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_MCMT))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_MCMT))
field_climate_08_23$MCMT_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$MCMT_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$MCMT_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$MCMT_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_MWMT_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_MWMT - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_MWMT))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_MWMT))
field_climate_08_23$MWMT_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$MWMT_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$MWMT_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$MWMT_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_MSP_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_MSP - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_MSP))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_MSP))
field_climate_08_23$MSP_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$MSP_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$MSP_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$MSP_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_TD_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_TD - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_TD))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_TD))
field_climate_08_23$TD_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$TD_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$TD_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$TD_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_SHM_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_SHM - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_SHM))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_SHM))
field_climate_08_23$SHM_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$SHM_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$SHM_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$SHM_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_MAP_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_MAP - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_MAP))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_MAP))
field_climate_08_23$MAP_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$MAP_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$MAP_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$MAP_dist))
field_climate_08_23$Site_MAT_std <- (field_climate_08_23$Site_MAT - mean(field_climate_08_23$Site_MAT))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$Site_MAT))
field_climate_08_23$MAT_dist_std <- (field_climate_08_23$MAT_dist - mean(field_climate_08_23$MAT_dist))/(2*sd(field_climate_08_23$MAT_dist))
```

## Compare models
List includes only models that converged/meet assumptions
```{r}
CC_modelsU  <- list(mCC_0_std,mCC_1_std, mCC_2_std, mCC_4_std, mCC_6_std,mCC_7_std, mCC_8_std,mCC_9_std, mCC_11_std,  mCC_13_std, mCC_15_std, mCC_165_std,  mCC_18_std,  mCC_22_std, mCC_23_std, mCC_24_std,mCC_25_std, mCC_26_std, mCC_27_std, mCC_28_std, mCC_29_std) 
mod.namesCCU <- c('mCC_0_std','mCC_1_std', 'mCC_2_std', 'mCC_4_std','mCC_6_std','mCC_7_std', 'mCC_8_std', 'mCC_9_std', 'mCC_11_std',  'mCC_13_std',  'mCC_15_std', 'mCC_165_std ', 'mCC_18_std',  'mCC_22_std', 'mCC_23_std', 'mCC_24_std','mCC_25_std','mCC_26_std',  'mCC_27_std', 'mCC_28_std', 'mCC_29_std') 

# Calculate AIC for each model 
CCmodels_aic_tableU <- aictab(cand.set = CC_modelsU, modnames=mod.namesCCU) 
print(CCmodels_aic_tableU)

# Selected model
summary(mCC_7_std)
```
